results.reason: Identifies §2.2's five-year auto-renewal and the 270/240-day notice window. Computes the window as Oct 3 to Nov 2, 2026. Explains lock-in for five more years with the MAPC step-up, and recommends a protective notice or a tolling amendment before the window closes.

Notes the §5.3 30-day objection right and deemed acceptance, receipt on Aug 21 and a deadline of about Sept 20. Says the right has likely lapsed, asks the client to confirm whether an objection was sent, and recommends seeking commercial relief.

Issue 5 covers the broad §11.1 indemnity reaching product-defect claims, its uncapped status under §12.3(a), and Brightmere's capped §11.2 indemnity. It recommends narrowing §11.1 to Halvorsen's fault.

Issue 4 explains that Amendment §3.1 replaces §12.3 and deletes the recall carve-out, so §9.3 reimbursement is now capped and a large recall could exceed the cap. It recommends restoring the carve-out.
Issue 3 identifies the Delaware law and Wilmington forum in Amendment §6, the conflict with §17, and that the amendment prevails under §1.4. It recommends restoring §17 (New York).
States the notice was delivered August 21, 2026.
States the Initial Term ends June 30, 2027.
States that written amendments rank first under §1.4.
Memo addressed to the partner. Each issue has Where, Why it matters and Recommended fix headings.
Concludes that recall reimbursement is now subject to the cap.
Acknowledges the Delaware provisions and concludes that Delaware likely governs.
